q: What is the correct formula for the theoretical probability P(E) of an event E?
o: Total outcomes / Favourable outcomes
Number of outcomes favourable to E / Total number of possible outcomes
Favourable outcomes × Total outcomes
1 - Favourable outcomes
e: Probability P(E) = (Number of outcomes favourable to E) / (Total number of possible outcomes of the experiment).

q: The probability P(E) of any event E always satisfies which inequality?
e: The probability of any event lies between 0 and 1 inclusive, so 0 ≤ P(E) ≤ 1.

q: What is the probability of a sure (certain) event?
e: An event that is certain to occur always has a probability equal to 1.

q: What is the probability of an impossible event?
o: Undefined
e: An event that cannot happen has 0 favourable outcomes, so its probability is 0.

q: What is the sum of the probabilities of all the elementary events of an experiment?
e: The sum of probabilities of all elementary events of an experiment is always 1.

q: What is the correct relation between an event E and its complementary event "not E" (Ē)?
e: The probabilities of an event and its complement always add up to 1: P(E) + P(Ē) = 1.

q: An event having only one outcome of the experiment is called:
o: Sure event
Impossible event
Elementary event
Complementary event
e: An event containing a single outcome of an experiment is called an elementary event.

q: Which of the following CANNOT be the probability of an event?
e: Probability of an event can never be negative (0 ≤ P(E) ≤ 1), so -1.5 cannot be a probability.

q: Which of the following cannot represent the probability of an event?
e: 105% = 1.05 > 1, and probability can never exceed 1 (or 100%).

q: If different outcomes of an experiment have the same chance of occurring, they are called:
o: Complementary outcomes
Equally likely outcomes
Impossible outcomes
Opposite outcomes
e: Outcomes that have equal chances of occurrence are called equally likely outcomes.

q: How many "face cards" are there in a standard deck of 52 playing cards?
e: There are 3 face cards (King, Queen, Jack) in each of the 4 suits, giving 4 × 3 = 12 face cards.

q: A standard deck of 52 playing cards is divided into how many suits, and how many cards are in each suit?
o: 2 suits, 26 cards each
4 suits, 13 cards each
13 suits, 4 cards each
4 suits, 12 cards each
e: A deck has 4 suits (Spades, Clubs, Hearts, Diamonds) with 13 cards in each suit.

q: How many red cards are there in a standard deck of 52 playing cards?
e: 13 Hearts and 13 Diamonds are red, making 26 red cards in total.

q: How many black face cards are there in a deck of 52 playing cards?
e: 3 face cards of Spades and 3 of Clubs are black, giving 6 black face cards.

q: How many Aces are there in a well-shuffled deck of 52 playing cards?
e: There is 1 Ace in each of the 4 suits, making 4 Aces in total.

q: How many total possible outcomes are there when two coins are tossed simultaneously?
e: Total possible outcomes = 2² = 4 (HH, HT, TH, TT).

q: What is the total number of possible outcomes when three coins are tossed simultaneously?
e: When three coins are tossed together, total outcomes = 2³ = 8.

q: How many total possible outcomes are obtained when two dice are thrown simultaneously?
e: Throwing two dice together gives 6 × 6 = 36 total possible outcomes.

q: If the probability of an event E is p, what is the probability of the complementary event "not E"?
o: p
e: P(E) + P(not E) = 1 ⇒ P(not E) = 1 - p.

q: In a single throw of a die, how many outcomes are favourable to getting a prime number?
e: The prime numbers on a die are 2, 3, and 5 (1 is not prime), so there are 3 favourable outcomes.

q: Getting a number greater than 6 in a single throw of an ordinary die is an example of:
o: Sure event
Impossible event
Elementary event
Equally likely event
e: A die only has faces 1 to 6, so getting a number greater than 6 is an impossible event.

q: Getting a natural number less than 7 in a single throw of an ordinary die is an example of:
o: Impossible event
Sure (Certain) event
Null event
Complementary event
e: All possible outcomes (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6) are less than 7, so it is a sure event.

Complementary event
Sure event
Impossible event
e: The event representing the non-occurrence of E ("not E") is called the complementary event of E.

q: How many red Kings are there in a deck of 52 playing cards?
e: There are 2 red Kings: King of Hearts and King of Diamonds.

q: In a single throw of a die, if E is the event of getting an even number and F is getting an odd number, what is P(E) + P(F)?
e: Since E and F are complementary events with P(E) = 1/2 and P(F) = 1/2, P(E) + P(F) = 1.

e: Probability of losing = 1 - 0.3 = 0.7.

q: Which value represents the probability of an impossible event?
e: The probability of an impossible event is 0.

Rare event

e: Probability of Reshma winning = 1 - 0.62 = 0.38.

q: Savita and Hamida are friends. What is the probability that both will have the same birthday? (Ignoring a leap year)
e: Out of 365 days, there is only 1 day matching Savita's birthday, so P(same birthday) = 1/365.

q: A die is thrown once. Find the probability of getting a prime number.
e: Prime numbers on a die are {2, 3, 5}, so P(prime) = 3/6 = 1/2.

q: A die is thrown once. What is the probability of getting a number lying between 2 and 6?
e: Numbers strictly between 2 and 6 are {3, 4, 5}, so probability = 3/6 = 1/2.

q: A die is thrown once. What is the probability of getting a number greater than 4?
e: Numbers greater than 4 are {5, 6}, so probability = 2/6 = 1/3.

q: Two coins are tossed simultaneously once. What is the probability of getting at least one head?
e: Outcomes are {HH, HT, TH, TT}. At least one head occurs in 3 cases, so P = 3/4.

q: A game consists of tossing a one-rupee coin 3 times. Hanif wins if all the tosses give the same result (3 heads or 3 tails), and loses otherwise. Find the probability that Hanif will lose the game.
e: Winning outcomes are {HHH, TTT} (2/8 = 1/4). Thus, probability of losing = 1 - 1/4 = 3/4.

q: One card is drawn from a well-shuffled deck of 52 cards. Find the probability of getting a king of red colour.
e: There are 2 red kings in a deck of 52 cards, so probability = 2/52 = 1/26.

q: One card is drawn at random from a deck of 52 cards. What is the probability of getting a face card?
e: Total face cards = 12. Probability = 12/52 = 3/13.

q: One card is drawn from a well-shuffled deck of 52 cards. Find the probability of getting the jack of hearts.
e: There is only 1 jack of hearts in a 52-card deck, so probability = 1/52.

q: A card is drawn at random from a deck of 52 cards. What is the probability that it is NOT an ace?
A bag contains 3 red balls and 5 black balls. A ball is drawn at random from the bag. What is the probability that the ball drawn is red?
e: Total balls = 3 + 5 = 8. Probability of a red ball = 3/8.

q: A box contains 5 red marbles, 8 white marbles, and 4 green marbles. One marble is taken out at random. What is the probability that it will NOT be green?
e: Total marbles = 17. Marbles that are not green = 5 + 8 = 13. Probability = 13/17.

q: A piggy bank contains hundred 50p coins, fifty ₹1 coins, twenty ₹2 coins, and ten ₹5 coins. If one coin falls out at random, what is the probability that it will be a 50p coin?
e: Total coins = 180. Probability of a 50p coin = 100/180 = 5/9.

q: Gopi buys a fish from a shop for his aquarium. The shopkeeper takes out one fish at random from a tank containing 5 male fish and 8 female fish. What is the probability that the fish taken out is a male fish?
e: Total fish = 5 + 8 = 13. Probability of male fish = 5/13.

q: A game of chance consists of spinning an arrow which comes to rest pointing at one of the numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 equally likely. What is the probability that it will point at a number greater than 2?
e: Numbers greater than 2 are {3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8}, so probability = 6/8 = 3/4.

q: A lot of 20 bulbs contains 4 defective ones. One bulb is drawn at random from the lot. What is the probability that this bulb is defective?
e: Probability of a defective bulb = 4 / 20 = 1 / 5.

q: A box contains 90 discs which are numbered from 1 to 90. If one disc is drawn at random from the box, find the probability that it bears a two-digit number.
e: Numbers from 10 to 90 are 81 two-digit numbers. Probability = 81 / 90 = 9 / 10.

q: One disc is drawn at random from 90 discs numbered 1 to 90. Find the probability that it bears a perfect square number.
e: Perfect squares from 1 to 90 are 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81 (9 numbers). Probability = 9/90 = 1/10.

q: A lot consists of 144 ball pens of which 20 are defective and the others are good. Nuri will buy a pen if it is good, and the shopkeeper draws one pen at random. What is the probability that she will buy it?
e: Good pens = 144 - 20 = 124. Probability of buying = 124/144 = 31/36.

q: A letter is chosen at random from the letters of the word "MATHEMATICS". What is the probability that the chosen letter is a vowel?
e: There are 11 letters in "MATHEMATICS", of which 4 are vowels (A, E, A, I). So probability = 4/11.

q: A letter is chosen at random from the 26 letters of the English alphabet. What is the probability that it is a consonant?
e: Out of 26 letters, 21 are consonants, so P(consonant) = 21/26.

q: In a single throw of a die, what is the probability of getting an even prime number?
e: The only even prime number on a die is 2, so probability = 1/6.

Two dice are thrown simultaneously. What is the probability of getting a sum equal to 7?

q: A card is drawn at random from a deck of 52 cards. What is the probability of getting the queen of diamonds?
e: There is only 1 queen of diamonds in 52 cards, so P = 1/52.

q: A child has a die whose six faces show the letters A, B, C, D, E, A. The die is thrown once. What is the probability of getting A?
e: A appears on 2 out of 6 faces, so probability = 2/6 = 1/3.

q: If P(E) = 3/7 for an event E, what is the value of P(not E)?
Three coins are tossed simultaneously. What is the probability of getting at most one tail?
e: At most 1 tail (0 or 1 tail): {HHH, HHT, HTH, THH} = 4 out of 8 outcomes. P = 4/8 = 1/2.

q: Three coins are tossed simultaneously. What is the probability of getting at least one tail?
e: Only {HHH} has no tail. So P(at least 1 tail) = 1 - 1/8 = 7/8.

q: Two dice are thrown simultaneously. What is the probability that the sum of numbers obtained is greater than 10?
A die is thrown twice. What is the probability that 5 will come up at least once?
e: Outcomes with no 5 = 5 × 5 = 25. Thus, P(5 at least once) = (36 - 25)/36 = 11/36.

q: A die is thrown twice. What is the probability that 5 will NOT come up either time?
e: Each throw has 5 choices other than 5, giving 5 × 5 = 25 pairs. Probability = 25/36.

q: Two dice are thrown simultaneously. What is the probability that the product of the two numbers is 12?
e: Pairs with product 12 are {(2,6), (3,4), (4,3), (6,2)} = 4 outcomes. P = 4/36 = 1/9.

q: Two dice are thrown simultaneously. What is the probability that the sum of the two numbers is a prime number?
e: Prime sums are 2(1), 3(2), 5(4), 7(6), 11(2) giving 15 favourable outcomes. P = 15/36 = 5/12.

q: Two dice are thrown together. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers is divisible by 5?
e: Sums divisible by 5 are 5 (4 pairs) and 10 (3 pairs), making 7/36.

q: Two dice are thrown simultaneously. What is the probability of getting odd numbers on both dice?
e: There are 3 odd numbers on each die, giving 3 × 3 = 9 pairs. Probability = 9/36 = 1/4.

q: Five cards—the ten, jack, queen, king, and ace of diamonds—are well-shuffled. First, a queen is drawn and put aside. If a second card is now picked up from the remaining cards, what is the probability that it is an ace?
e: After putting the queen aside, 4 cards remain including 1 ace. Thus, probability = 1/4.

q: All red face cards are removed from a pack of 52 playing cards. From the remaining cards, a card is drawn at random. Find the probability that it is a red card.
e: After removing 6 red face cards, remaining cards = 46 and remaining red cards = 20. Probability = 20/46 = 10/23.

q: The king, queen, and jack of clubs are removed from a deck of 52 playing cards and then well shuffled. One card is selected from the remaining cards. Find the probability of getting a heart.
e: 3 club cards are removed, leaving 49 cards while all 13 hearts remain. Thus P(heart) = 13/49.

q: All black kings and black queens are removed from a deck of 52 cards. A card is drawn at random from the remaining cards. What is the probability of getting a face card?
e: 4 black face cards removed ⇒ 48 cards remain with 12 - 4 = 8 face cards. P = 8/48 = 1/6.

q: Suppose you drop a die at random on a rectangular region measuring 3 m by 2 m, which contains a circular area of diameter 1 m inside it. What is the probability that it will land inside the circle?
e: Circle radius = 0.5 m, area = π/4 m². Rectangle area = 6 m². Probability = (π/4)/6 = π/24.

q: A bag contains 24 balls of which x are red, 2x are white, and 3x are blue. A ball is selected at random. What is the probability that it is NOT red?
e: 6x = 24 ⇒ x = 4. So 4 balls are red and 20 are not red. P(not red) = 20/24 = 5/6.

q: A box contains 12 balls out of which x are black. If 6 more black balls are put in the box, the probability of drawing a black ball becomes double of what it was before. Find x.
A jar contains 24 marbles, some are green and others are blue. If a marble is drawn at random, the probability that it is green is 2/3. Find the number of blue marbles in the jar.
e: P(blue) = 1 - 2/3 = 1/3. Number of blue marbles = (1/3) × 24 = 8.

q: Cards marked with numbers 5 to 50 are placed in a box. A card is drawn at random. Find the probability that the number on the card is divisible by 5.
e: Total cards = 50 - 5 + 1 = 46. Multiples of 5 from 5 to 50 are 10. Probability = 10/46 = 5/23.

q: A card is drawn at random from a box containing cards numbered from 11 to 60. Find the probability that the number is a multiple of 7.
e: Total cards = 50. Multiples of 7 between 11 and 60 are {14, 21, 28, 35, 42, 49, 56} (7 cards). P = 7/50.

q: Cards numbered 2 to 101 are placed in a box. One card is drawn at random. Find the probability that the number on the card is a prime number less than 20.
A disc is drawn at random from 90 discs numbered 1 to 90. What is the probability that it bears a number divisible by 5?
e: Multiples of 5 from 1 to 90 = 18. Probability = 18/90 = 1/5.

q: What is the probability of having 53 Sundays in a randomly chosen non-leap year?
e: A non-leap year has 52 full weeks and 1 extra day, which can be any of the 7 days. So P(53 Sundays) = 1/7.

q: What is the probability of having 53 Sundays in a randomly selected leap year?
e: A leap year has 52 weeks + 2 extra consecutive days (7 pairs, 2 containing Sunday). So P = 2/7.

q: A number x is chosen at random from -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3. What is the probability that |x| < 2?
e: Out of 7 numbers, {-1, 0, 1} satisfy |x| < 2. Thus, P(|x| < 2) = 3/7.

q: If a number x is chosen at random from -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, what is the probability that x² ≤ 1?
e: Out of 5 numbers, {-1, 0, 1} satisfy x² ≤ 1. Probability = 3/5.

q: A bag contains 5 red balls and some blue balls. If the probability of drawing a blue ball is three times that of drawing a red ball, find the number of blue balls in the bag.
e: Let blue balls be x. Then x/(5+x) = 3 × [5/(5+x)] ⇒ x = 15.

q: Two dice are thrown simultaneously. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers appearing on them is 8?
If P(E) - P(not E) = 0.2 for an event E, find the value of P(E).
e: Adding P(E) + P(not E) = 1 and P(E) - P(not E) = 0.2 gives 2P(E) = 1.2 ⇒ P(E) = 0.6.

q: A carton consists of 100 shirts of which 88 are good, 8 have minor defects, and 4 have major defects. Sujata, a trader, only rejects the shirts with major defects. One shirt is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is acceptable to Sujata?
e: Acceptable shirts to Sujata = 88 + 8 = 96. Thus probability = 96/100 = 0.96.

q: A lot of 20 bulbs contains 4 defective ones. Suppose the first bulb drawn is not defective and is not replaced. Now one bulb is drawn at random from the rest. What is the probability that this bulb is NOT defective?
e: After 1 good bulb is removed without replacement, 15 good out of 19 bulbs remain. So P = 15/19.

q:
[Case Study 1] Rohan and his friend are playing a probability game with a well-shuffled deck of 52 playing cards. One card is drawn at random.

What is the probability that the drawn card is a black face card?
e: Black face cards = 6 (3 Spades + 3 Clubs). Probability = 6/52 = 3/26.

q:
[Case Study 1] One card is drawn at random from a well-shuffled deck of 52 cards:

What is the probability that it is neither a King nor a Queen?
e: There are 4 Kings and 4 Queens (8 cards). Remaining = 52 - 8 = 44. P = 44/52 = 11/13.

q:
[Case Study 1] One card is drawn at random from a well-shuffled deck of 52 cards:

What is the probability of getting a Spade or an Ace?
e: 13 Spades + 3 remaining Aces = 16 cards (since Ace of Spades is common). P = 16/52 = 4/13.

q:
[Case Study 1] One card is drawn at random from a well-shuffled deck of 52 cards:

What is the probability of getting a red Jack?
e: There are 2 red Jacks (Hearts and Diamonds). Probability = 2/52 = 1/26.

q: [Case Study 1] If all 4 Jacks are removed from the deck of 52 cards and kept aside, what is the probability of drawing a red card from the remaining deck?
e: Removing 4 Jacks (2 red, 2 black) leaves 48 cards with 24 red cards. Probability = 24/48 = 1/2.

q:
[Case Study 2] In a board game, two standard dice (one blue and one grey) are thrown at the same time and the numbers appearing on their top faces are noted.

What is the total number of possible outcomes in this experiment?
e: For two dice, total possible outcomes = 6 × 6 = 36.

q:
[Case Study 2] When two standard dice are thrown simultaneously:

What is the probability of getting the same number on both dice (a doublet)?
e: There are 6 doublets out of 36 outcomes, so P = 6/36 = 1/6.

q:
[Case Study 2] When two standard dice are thrown simultaneously:

What is the probability that the sum of the two numbers is 9?
e: Pairs summing to 9 are {(3,6), (4,5), (5,4), (6,3)} = 4 outcomes. P = 4/36 = 1/9.

q:
[Case Study 2] When two standard dice are thrown simultaneously:

What is the probability that the sum of the two numbers is a multiple of 3?
e: Sums divisible by 3 are 3(2), 6(5), 9(4), 12(1) = 12 outcomes. P = 12/36 = 1/3.

q:
[Case Study 2] When two standard dice are thrown simultaneously:

What is the probability of getting an even number on the first die and an odd number on the second die?
e: 3 even choices for first die and 3 odd choices for second die give 3 × 3 = 9 outcomes. P = 9/36 = 1/4.

q: Two dice are thrown simultaneously. What is the probability of getting a sum of at least 10?
e: Sums ≥ 10 are 10 (3 pairs), 11 (2 pairs), 12 (1 pair) = 6 outcomes. P = 6/36 = 1/6.

q: Two dice are thrown simultaneously. What is the probability that the product of the numbers obtained is less than 9?
e: Favourable pairs: 6 + 4 + 2 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 16 out of 36. Probability = 16/36 = 4/9.

q: Three coins are tossed simultaneously. What is the probability of getting at least two consecutive heads?
e: Out of 8 outcomes, {HHH, HHT, THH} have at least two consecutive heads (3 outcomes). P = 3/8.

q: A bag contains 15 white balls and some black balls. If the probability of drawing a black ball is thrice that of a white ball, find the number of black balls in the bag.
e: Number of black balls = 3 × number of white balls = 3 × 15 = 45.

q: A bag contains 18 balls out of which x balls are red. If 2 more red balls are put in the bag, the probability of drawing a red ball will be 9/8 times that of drawing a red ball earlier. Find x.
A circular dartboard of radius 14 cm has a central bullseye circle of radius 3.5 cm. If a dart hits the board at random, what is the probability that it hits the bullseye?

A missing helicopter is reported to have crashed somewhere in a 9 km × 4.5 km rectangular region containing a lake of dimensions 3 km × 2.5 km. What is the probability that it crashed inside the lake?
e: Lake area = 7.5 km², total area = 40.5 km². Probability = 7.5 / 40.5 = 5 / 27.

q: A number x is selected from {1, 2, 3} and then a second number y is randomly selected from {1, 4, 9}. What is the probability that the product xy is less than 9?
e: Out of 9 pairs, xy < 9 for (1,1), (1,4), (2,1), (2,4), (3,1), i.e., 5 pairs. Probability = 5/9.

q: Two customers Shyam and Ekta visit a particular shop in the same week (Tuesday to Saturday). What is the probability that both will visit the shop on consecutive days?
e: Total pairs = 25. Consecutive pairs (both orders) = 4 + 4 = 8. Probability = 8/25.

q: Shyam and Ekta visit a shop randomly during the same week (Tuesday to Saturday, 5 days). What is the probability that both visit on different days?
e: P(same day) = 5/25 = 1/5, so P(different days) = 1 - 1/5 = 4/5.

q: If four unbiased coins are tossed simultaneously, what is the probability of getting exactly 2 heads?
e: Total outcomes = 16. Exactly 2 heads occur in 6 outcomes (HHTT, HTHT, HTTH, THHT, THTH, TTHH). P = 6/16 = 3/8.

q: A natural number is chosen at random from 1 to 50. What is the probability that it is either a prime number or a multiple of 10?
e: There are 15 primes and 5 multiples of 10 from 1 to 50 (disjoint). Total = 20/50 = 2/5.

q: What is the probability that a randomly selected non-leap year has 53 Tuesdays OR 53 Wednesdays?
e: The single extra day must be either Tuesday or Wednesday out of 7 days, giving probability 2/7.

q: What is the probability that a leap year selected at random will contain BOTH 53 Sundays and 53 Mondays?
e: Of the 7 possible pairs of extra consecutive days, only (Sunday, Monday) includes both. Thus P = 1/7.

q: What is the probability that a leap year selected at random will contain 53 Sundays OR 53 Mondays?
e: Out of 7 pairs of consecutive days, {(Sat,Sun), (Sun,Mon), (Mon,Tue)} give at least one Sunday or Monday. P = 3/7.

q: A letter is chosen at random from the word "ASSASSINATION". What is the probability that it is a vowel?
e: Out of 13 letters, 6 are vowels (A, A, A, I, I, O). Probability = 6/13.

q: A two-digit number is chosen at random. What is the probability that the sum of its digits is 9?
e: Out of 90 two-digit numbers, 9 numbers {18,27,36,45,54,63,72,81,90} have digit sum 9. P = 9/90 = 1/10.

q: A two-digit number is chosen at random. What is the probability that it is divisible by both 3 and 4?
e: Multiples of LCM(3,4) = 12 among two-digit numbers are 8 (12 to 96). Probability = 8/90 = 4/45.

q: One ticket is drawn at random from a bag containing tickets numbered 1 to 40. Find the probability that the selected ticket has a number which is a multiple of 5 or 7.
e: Multiples of 5 (8) + multiples of 7 (5) - common multiple 35 (1) = 12. P = 12/40 = 3/10.

q: If P(E) = x/3 and P(not E) = 2/5 for an event E, what is the value of x?
The probability of guessing the correct answer to a certain test question is x/12. If the probability of not guessing the correct answer is 2/3, then find x.
If the probability of winning a game is x/3 and losing it is x/2 (no draw), find x.
Two dice are thrown simultaneously. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers on both dice is a perfect square?
e: Perfect squares between 2 and 12 are 4 (3 pairs) and 9 (4 pairs), giving 7/36.

q: A jar contains only red, blue, and green marbles. The probability of selecting a red marble is 1/4 and a blue marble is 1/3. If the jar contains 10 green marbles, how many total marbles are in the jar?
All Aces and all Kings are removed from a deck of 52 playing cards. One card is drawn at random from the remaining deck. What is the probability that it is a black Queen?
e: Removing 4 Aces and 4 Kings leaves 44 cards with 2 black Queens. P = 2/44 = 1/22.

q: All red cards are removed from a deck of 52 playing cards. One card is drawn at random from the remaining cards. What is the probability that it is a face card?
e: Among the remaining 26 black cards, there are 6 black face cards. Probability = 6/26 = 3/13.

q: A card is drawn at random from a well-shuffled deck of 52 playing cards. What is the probability that the card drawn is neither a spade nor a jack?
e: 13 spades + 3 other jacks = 16 cards excluded. Remaining = 52 - 16 = 36. P = 36/52 = 9/13.

q: An integer is chosen at random between 1 and 100 (inclusive). What is the probability that it is NOT divisible by 8?
e: 12 integers from 1 to 100 are divisible by 8 (8 to 96). So 88 are not divisible. P = 88/100 = 22/25.

q: A bag contains 5 white, 7 red, 4 black, and 2 blue balls. One ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is neither white nor black?
e: Total balls = 18. Balls neither white nor black = 7 red + 2 blue = 9. P = 9/18 = 1/2.

q: Two fair dice are rolled giving outcomes a and b. What is the probability that |a - b| ≥ 3?
e: Pairs with |a-b|=3 (6), |a-b|=4 (4), and |a-b|=5 (2) total 12 out of 36. P = 12/36 = 1/3.
